question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt `channels.msteams.accounts` and `channels.msteams.defaultAccount` as its public multi-bot contract, with legacy root configuration remaining the implicit default account and named accounts requiring explicit bot identity and webhook port?
rationale: The patch is technically strong and proven, but it creates compatibility-sensitive public configuration, credential inheritance, listener, and persistent-state semantics that require Teams-area product ownership.

options.title: Accept account map
options.body: Approve the proposed account map, implicit legacy default, explicit named-account identity/listener requirements, and per-account auth and state isolation.

options.title: Revise contract first
options.body: Require specific schema, listener multiplexing, credential inheritance, or migration changes before exposing the public API.

options.title: Pause for shared design
options.body: Defer this branch if maintainers want a broader cross-channel account contract before adding Teams support.

recommendation.title: Accept account map
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed account map, implicit legacy default, explicit named-account identity/listener requirements, and per-account auth and state isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: Brad Groux has extensive merged Teams feature history and is the person explicitly asked in the PR discussion to accept or revise this Microsoft Teams contract.
